statement: The critical-extinction assertion cannot include p_c=1: for the nearest-neighbour graph on Z, Bernoulli bond percolation has p_c=1 and P_1(|C(0)|=infinity)=1.
assumptions: G is the nearest-neighbour graph on Z
source: Owner work: elementary boundary calculation; local ranking omits the p_c<1 qualification in its P0043 short title, while C0084 includes it.
proof: For p<1 the probability that all n edges from 0 to n are open is p^n tending to 0; the same holds to the left. An infinite connected subset containing 0 must be unbounded in at least one direction, so theta(p)=0. At p=1 every edge is open and the entire graph is connected.

statement: For a rooted spherically symmetric tree with a_i in {1,2} children at depth i, independent bond parameter 0<p<=1, terminal depth n, and m_j=p^j product_(i<j)a_i, the root survival probability q_0^(n) satisfies 1/m_n+S_n/4 <= 1/q_0^(n) <= 1/m_n+S_n/[4(1-p/2)], where S_n=sum_(i<n:a_i=2)1/m_i.
source: owner-own-work; derivation in ATTEMPT.md Lemma A; a standard varying-environment branching calculation, no novelty claim
proof: q_i=pq_(i+1) if a_i=1 and q_i=2pq_(i+1)-p^2q_(i+1)^2 if a_i=2, justified by disjoint descendant subtrees. Set d_i=0 in the first case and d_i=1/[4(1-pq_(i+1)/2)] in the second. Telescoping gives 1/q_0=1/m_n+sum_i d_i/m_i; bound each nonzero d_i between 1/4 and 1/[4(1-p/2)].

statement: For beta real, N=ceil(8(1+|beta|)), B_n=floor(n/2+beta log_2(1+n/N)), and offspring a_n=2^(B_(n+1)-B_n), the resulting infinite rooted tree T_beta has maximum degree at most 3 and critical Bernoulli bond probability 1/sqrt(2). At criticality theta_o>0 iff beta>1. Critical root one-arm probability to level n is comparable to n^(beta-1) for beta<1, and to 1/log n for beta=1. Every T_beta is outside the quasi-transitive target class.
assumptions: deterministic rooted spherically symmetric tree as defined
source: owner-own-work; ATTEMPT.md Main special case, based on C02
proof: The smooth exponent has derivative in (1/4,3/4), so offspring are 1 or 2 and every block of four levels branches. L_n is within a factor 2 of sqrt(2)^n(1+n/N)^beta. Below 1/sqrt(2), E Z_n tends to zero; above it the reciprocal bound C02 gives positive survival. At criticality S_n is comparable to sum_(i<n)(1+i/N)^(-beta), giving convergence exactly for beta>1 and the stated divergence rates otherwise. The root is the unique leaf, so all automorphisms fix it; infinitely many distance levels imply infinitely many vertex orbits.

statement: There are infinite connected rooted trees of maximum degree 3, all with critical probability exactly 1/sqrt(2), whose critical root survival probabilities are zero and whose local limit has strictly positive critical root survival. Hence equality/convergence of p_c does not allow critical extinction to pass to local limits of arbitrary bounded-degree rooted graphs.
proof: Take T_2 from C03 and let T^(K) agree on the first K offspring levels, then alternate 1,2 children forever. In each periodic tail the critical means are bounded above and below while infinitely many levels branch, so C02 gives extinction; the same exponential growth gives p_c=1/sqrt(2). The rooted balls converge to T_2, whose critical survival is positive by C03.

statement: Every T_beta in C03 is quasi-isometric to the rooted binary tree. In particular T_0 and T_2 are quasi-isometric connected trees of degree at most 3 with equal critical bond probability 1/sqrt(2), yet critical extinction holds only for T_0. Critical extinction is therefore not a quasi-isometry invariant for arbitrary bounded-degree graphs, even with equal critical parameters.
proof: Contract unary corridors to the full binary branching skeleton. Every corridor and the initial stem have length at most 4.
